report.headline: The "+8–15% momentum entry" thesis shows no demonstrated edge on daily bars.
report.screener_note: The screener (gate-pass alerts, no score) is what ships. This report explains why it makes no predictive claim.

research_round_1.title: Research round 1 — the only round (stopping rule applied)

hypotheses.label: Path-aware labels (first-passage) are less volatility-dominated than touch-anytime
hypotheses.reason: Refuted by its own control — every feature that cleared the bar on the new label cleared it just as well on the old one.

hypotheses.label: A shorter horizon (+20% in 10 sessions) suits a daily-bar signal
hypotheses.verdict_note: Cleared its written bar arithmetically — NOT counted. The passing feature (atr_pct) was the stratification variable itself, and it scored WORSE on this label than on the original one.
hypotheses.reason: A flaw in how the rule was written (its feature set contains the stratifier), not a real finding. Not counting it was the user's ruling, made after seeing the table and the control.

hypotheses.label: Relative sector strength conditions which movers follow through
hypotheses.reason: Flat. One of the cleanest negative results in the project.

hypotheses.label: Market regime (SPY/IWM/VIX) conditions the base rate
hypotheses.reason: Flat across all three regime inputs tested.

abandoned.label: Catalyst via Tiingo News
abandoned.reason: Tiingo News is a ~3-month archive against Finnhub's ~12 — would have reduced coverage, not extended it. Abandoned before the round ran; no substitute hypothesis added.

sample_size.excludes: the lockbox region and the in-sample pilot window

closing_statement: Everything that looked like signal across Phases 1 and 2 — the v2 score, rvol, rvol inside ATR terciles, and atr_pct on three new labels — reduced to the same thing: volatile and low-priced stocks make large percentage moves more often, and nothing tested here says which ones or when.
